bullets.title: AI trade unwinds sharply: NDX -2%, semis -20% from June peak on China competition fears
bullets.body: China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3 (2.8T param, top-3 globally in benchmarks), triggering a 'DeepSeek 2.0' narrative. NDX futures fell ~2% overnight; NVDA -2.7%, AMD -3.8%, GOOGL -4.4%, semis down ~20% from June highs per Jefferies, with the 30-day drawdown exceeding dot-com era on this timeframe. HF gross leverage remains near 99th percentile 5yr, and positioning is not fully washed out (-0.4z vs -1 to -2z for a clean reset.

bullets.title: NFLX -9-11% on soft 3Q guide and reduced engagement disclosure
bullets.body: Netflix Q2 revenue $12.56B (slight miss) with EPS $0.80 beat, but 3Q revenue guidance $12.86B missed consensus $13.00B and FCF came in at $1.53B vs. ~$2.7B est. Management is shifting 'What We Watched' from semi-annual to annual disclosure starting 2027, which the Street reads negatively. Multiple banks cut price targets; JPM cut to $85, Wolfe to $84, MS to $83; median PT fell ~6% to ~$106. Bull case rests on <45% broadband HH penetration, $3B ad revenue doubling, and $27B buyback authorization.

bullets.title: Asia markets in freefall: Nikkei -5%, Taiwan -6%, record $5.8B Taiwan equity outflows
bullets.body: Japanese stocks entered technical correction (>10% from June ATH); Nikkei closed down ~5%, Taiwan Taiex fell 6.5% (3-sigma move). Foreign investors sold a record $5.8B in Taiwan shares. Kioxia halved from June peak and hit daily limit-down. South Korea saw 1.2M retail margin calls (3.4% of adult population). Asia-focused L/S hedge funds were down 11.7% MTD per Goldman prime.

bullets.title: Fed on hold through 2026; Jefferson flags AI-inflation risk and energy-trade policy dilemma
bullets.body: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson reiterated data-dependence and the 2% inflation mandate, warning that if inflation doesn't resume cooling the Fed may need to reconsider its stance. He flagged AI as a dual-sided risk (demand could lift inflation before productivity offsets it) and noted overlapping energy/trade shocks risk entrenching expectations. Dallas Fed's Logan also sounded hawkish. MS base case: Fed holds all of 2026, cuts 50bp in 2027.

bullets.title: 10Y UST sticky around 4.52%; G7 yields moving homogeneously higher
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield edged up ~4bps to 4.52% despite dovish CPI/PPI prints. Analysts attribute stickiness to persistent inflation risk, fiscal deficits, and stronger-than-expected growth (+2% real consumption). G7 sovereign yields described as moving together toward a higher-rate regime. September Fed hike is characterized as a 'coin flip.'

bullets.title: ECB expected to hold next week, with final hike in September
bullets.body: JPM previews ECB as very likely on hold at next week's meeting, with a neutral-to-slightly-hawkish statement. A final 25bp hike is expected in September; a December third hike is possible but less certain. Core Eurozone inflation remains sticky at 2.4% YoY, and energy price risks are tilted to the upside given Strait of Hormuz tensions.

bullets.title: Middle East escalation: US conducts sixth consecutive night of Iran strikes; Hormuz throughput -42%
bullets.body: US CENTCOM confirmed new strikes against Iran for a sixth consecutive night, targeting naval capabilities and coastal surveillance sites. Iran's IRGC claimed attacks on US assets in Jordan, Kuwait, and Bahrain. Crude flows through the Strait of Hormuz fell to ~5.5M bpd from 9.4M bpd. WTI crude rose +$1.90 to ~$80.18 intraday; Brent settled at $84.23 (-0.85%). Gold climbed ~1% to $4,008/oz.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler 2027 capex bars at $1.1T median; AI debt issuance $311B in 1H26
bullets.body: Buyside median 2027 hyperscaler capex survey sits at $1.1T (range $1-1.7T), with 68% of investors expecting actuals to come in above their stated concern threshold. Hyperscaler 2027 capex bars tracked by JPM are even higher: GOOGL $325-350B vs. street $250B, AMZN $300B vs. $230B, META $200-225B vs. $170B. AI-related debt issuance hit $311B in 1H26, tracking toward $580B for full year.

bullets.title: Kimi K3 bull-bear debate: competitive threat vs. commodity intelligence benefiting hyperscalers
bullets.body: Jefferies' AI bull-bear frame: bears note 70-85% of AI compute serves two unprofitable labs with circular financing, open-source models 50% cheaper, and broken unit economics ($200/month plans consuming $8-14K tokens). Bulls counter with $2T contracted backlog vs. $784B spent and AI at <5% of software revenue. JPM and others note that fragmented model competition (Kimi, DeepSeek, Qwen) positions hyperscalers as orchestration layer winners regardless of which model leads.

bullets.title: Memory sector drawdown historic but long-only positioning not fully washed out
bullets.body: The Memory Index (MSXXGMEM) fell >10% Thursday and is down 36% from its June 22nd peak. CRWV -53%, MRVL -44%, ARM -44%, WDC -43% from 52-week highs per Jefferies. Despite the pain, long-only managers have only marginally reduced semi/memory exposure; combined 6-month z-score at only -0.4z vs. -1 to -2z for a clean washout. Weekly momentum indicators remain overbought, implying further downside risk per technical analysis.

bullets.title: BOJ holds rates in July; GPIF shifting to domestic assets as yen weakens
bullets.body: BOJ is expected to keep rates unchanged at its July meeting per Kyodo. Japanese Finance Minister Katayama signaled readiness to intervene in FX markets if needed. PM Takaichi highlighted GPIF accumulation of domestic assets as a key initiative, with the pension fund rebalancing from foreign to domestic in response to yen depreciation.

bullets.title: GOOGL Gemini 3.5 Pro delayed months; internal frustration rising over competitive losses
bullets.body: Google's Gemini 3.5 Pro launch has been pushed back by months after failing to meet internal performance goals in coding. Bloomberg and multiple sources report growing frustration among Google engineers and managers about losing ground to Anthropic and OpenAI. The stock fell 4.4% on Thursday, erasing ~$200B in market cap.

bullets.title: HSBC upgrades AAPL to Buy, PT $366 from $260 (41% upside); stock hits ATH
bullets.body: HSBC analyst Nicolas Cote-Colisson upgraded Apple to Buy from Hold and raised the price target to $366 from $260, implying ~41% upside from current levels of ~$333. The stock hit a new all-time high during Thursday's session and is approximately $100B away from a $5 trillion market cap, which would make it only the second company to reach that milestone.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Healthcare, REITs, energy outperform as tech momentum unwinds
bullets.body: With the high-beta momentum basket down 28.9% over the past month and the High Retail Investor Sentiment basket down 12.1%, capital is rotating into defensive and yield-oriented names. XLV and XLRE outperformed by 2%+ on Thursday. Oil/energy names outperformed on crude strength (+2.4% WTI intraday), while financials continued to beat driven by strong regional bank earnings (TFC, RF beats; FITB roughly in-line).

bullets.title: Single-stock volatility vs. index vol at dot-com-era highs; JPM remains tactically bullish
bullets.body: Single-stock volatility relative to index volatility has surged to its highest level since the dot-com bubble per multiple sources. JPM's US Morning Intelligence desk remains 'Tactically Bullish,' citing benign CPI/PPI, strong consumer data (Philly Fed 41.1 vs. 10.3 prior, jobless claims 208K), and solid Financial sector earnings as support. Key risks cited include Middle East escalation, bond yield spikes during earnings season, and momentum de-leveraging continuing.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 profit +77%; raises 2026 capex guide to $60-64B but stock fell 3.8%
bullets.body: TSMC reported Q2 revenue of $40.2B (+33.7% YoY, top of guidance) and gross margin of 67.7% (beating its 65.5-67.5% guided range). AI semiconductor revenue is now tracking above its prior 55-60% CAGR forecast, with analysts modeling 70-80% CAGR as reasonable. However, the stock fell 3.8% in Taiwan and ADRs also declined as investors focused on higher capex ($60-64B vs prior $52-56B) and sustained selling of the broader semiconductor sector.

bullets.title: Huawei 950 SuperPoD & Kimi K3 highlight China hardware independence trajectory
bullets.body: Huawei released its 950 SuperPoD offering 1 EFLOPS at FP8 and 2 EFLOPS at FP4 with 256TB unified memory, directly challenging NVIDIA's DGX family. Separately, Jensen Huang has flagged the risk that Chinese AI models could specialize toward Huawei chips rather than NVIDIA, representing a structural threat to NVIDIA's long-term moat. Lawmakers are also urging Commerce to maintain restrictions on Chinese DRAM players (CXMT, YMT).

bullets.title: Macro data supportive but insufficient to drive yields lower
bullets.body: Jobless claims fell to 208K (prior 216K) and Philly Fed Manufacturing surged to 41.1 from 10.3, pointing to resilient US growth. Despite cooler June CPI/PPI prints, 10Y yields remain sticky around 4.52% as the market prices growth too strong for sharper Fed cuts. The US dollar is tracking for a weekly loss as rate-hike bets are scaled back slightly, while gold is near $4,008/oz.

bullets.title: META hires top AWS executive Dave Brown for cloud/data center buildout
bullets.body: Meta has poached Dave Brown, one of Amazon's most senior computing executives (~20 years experience), to lead its data center and infrastructure buildout. The move is viewed as preparation for a potential 'MetAWS' cloud push. MS notes a META cloud business launch would increase colocation demand, benefiting EQIX and DLR.

bullets.title: Next week earnings: GOOGL, TXN, AMD AI event, INTC, NOW, GEV all in focus
bullets.body: Key earnings next week include GOOGL (Wed 7/22 after close, consensus EPS $2.88 / rev $117B), TXN (Wed 7/22, Citi models 4-13% EPS upside), INTC (Thu 7/23, data center CPU beat expected), and NOW (Wed 7/22, investors watching for cRPO growth >18.5%). AMD hosts its Advancing AI conference July 22-23 with potential MI455X announcements and new LLM customer (Meta GPU ramp); also TSLA and GEV reporting.
